solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Intimate conclusion of plot not revealed

parts.note: intimate friends are close friends

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, so take the end of plot

explanation.surface: A thriller writer keeps the ending of the plot under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intimate conclusion' reads as one phrase about an ending; it splits into 'Intimate' and 'conclusion of plot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Closet as an adjective means secret or hidden, as in a closet fan who never admits it.

clue.text: Were pound to plummet, this contract could provide support

indicators.note: in a down entry, plummeting sends a letter from the top of the column to the bottom

parts.note: an easel supports a painter's canvas
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A tenant worries that a currency crash could leave their agreement as their only prop.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is told backwards: drop the L at the top of the answer to the foot of the column and you get the support, EASEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a contract letting property for a set term, so 'this contract' names it.

clue.text: Extra information from border not amounting to much

parts.note: a side is an edge or border
something light is slight or trivial

explanation.surface: An unimportant footnote from the margin of a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is incidental information that illuminates a subject from an unexpected angle.

clue.text: Bitten by sheep, a graduate leaves under wraps

indicators.note: being bitten by something means having its teeth around you, so the sheep's letters enclose the rest

parts.note: a teg is a sheep in its second year
BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate, nipped by a sheep, slips away quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb about the graduate departing; it is the noun, tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea bag holds tea leaves wrapped in a porous paper pouch.

clue.text: Seabird crossing land offshore to find vegetation

indicators.note: the seabird's letters cross over, spanning the land offshore

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
a reef is a ridge of rock or coral lying offshore

explanation.surface: A seabird flies over an offshore reef in search of greenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree fern is a large tropical plant, so it is a kind of vegetation.

clue.text: Fifty percent of members bound to participate in this event?

definitions.text: Fifty percent of members bound to participate in this event?

parts.words: Fifty percent of members bound to participate in this event?
parts.note: in this sports-day race pairs run with one leg each tied together, so half of the runners' legs (members) are bound

explanation.surface: A survey about how many club members must enter a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' means limbs, not club members, and 'bound' means tied, not obliged.
explanation.definitionFit: In this school sports race, partners run with adjacent legs tied, so half their limbs are bound.

clue.text: I didn't quite catch that dance

definitions.meaning: a polite request to repeat something not heard
a dance in which one may cut in on a couple and take a partner

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite apology for mishearing, and is also the name of a partner-swapping ballroom dance.

clue.text: More than one prime game

definitions.meaning: five is a prime number, so several of it are plural primes
a court game in which a ball is struck with the gloved hand, played at English schools

explanation.definitionFit: Five is a prime number, so the plural names several primes; it is also an English handball game.

clue.text: Rogue trader ballyhoo accompanies always

parts.note: ballyhoo is noisy fuss, a racket
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A dodgy dealer is forever surrounded by hype.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs dishonest schemes for money, a crooked dealer or rogue.

clue.text: Treating children terribly, a patricide

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly treated and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A grim headline: someone treating children has killed their father.
explanation.definitionFit: Paediatric medicine is the branch concerned with caring for young patients.

clue.text: Two couples rejected church's corruption

indicators.note: rejected things are thrown back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: two couples make four, IV in Roman numerals
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Two couples spurned by the church for their sinfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: Two couples make four, written in Roman numerals before being turned round by 'rejected'.
explanation.definitionFit: Vice is wickedness or depravity, a moral corruption.

clue.text: You need time to get to know this fellow

definitions.text: You need time to get to know this fellow

parts.words: You need time to get to know this fellow
parts.note: time here means a prison sentence: you must be doing time to share quarters with this companion

explanation.surface: Friendships take a while to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' looks like patience in a friendship; it is prison time.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellmate is a fellow prisoner sharing a cell, met only by serving a sentence.

clue.text: Region and former kingdom — it's east of South America

indicators.note: on a map east lies to the right, so in an across entry this piece comes after the rest

parts.note: US stands for the United States, America
it is a dated word for sex appeal; the 's is just is

explanation.surface: A geography quiz locating somewhere east of South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South America' is not the continent but S plus US. SUSSEX is an English county, once an Anglo-Saxon kingdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Sussex is a county in southern England that was formerly the kingdom of the South Saxons.

clue.text: One-time radical husband attempting to conceal baldness?

indicators.note: the hairpiece is wrapped around the husband, hiding him inside

parts.note: a wig is what tries to cover baldness, so baldness by extension gives its cover

explanation.surface: A husband tries to hide going bald.
explanation.walkthrough: The wig 'attempting to conceal baldness' is read twice: as the wrapper and as the thing named.
explanation.definitionFit: The Whigs were the reforming party of 18th and 19th century British politics, radicals in their day.

clue.text: Woman consumer stopped by force some time later

parts.note: her refers to a woman

indicators.note: the consumer's letters are plugged by the force letter, which sits inside them

parts.note: an eater consumes food
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A female shopper halted by police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumer' looks like a shopper; it is an EATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereafter means from now on, at a future time.

clue.text: Delivery of first Christmas meal, menu having changed

indicators.note: a changed set of letters has been rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A caterer delivering the first Christmas dinner under a revised menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having changed' rearranges MEAL and MENU together. 'Delivery' is the baby born, not a food drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel, meaning God with us, is a name for the Christ child born at the first Christmas.

clue.text: Horrific experience in Black Sea for Caesar

parts.note: night is black, dark
mare is Latin, Caesar's language, for sea

explanation.surface: Caesar endures something dreadful on the Black Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a terrifying dream, and by extension any horrific ordeal.

clue.text: Officer holding strange belief makes provision for safety aboard

indicators.note: the officer's letters hold the rest between them

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of belief are made odd, jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship's officer with odd convictions takes charge of safety measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is a link; 'strange' is the anagram signal and 'holding' places the jumble inside the lieutenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifebelt is a buoyant ring kept on a ship to keep a person afloat.

clue.text: Horse in literature in contortions through pain

indicators.note: in says the horse letter goes inside the literature

parts.note: writing is literature
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A horse in a story twists in agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is heroin, H in drug slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Writhing means twisting and squirming, as one does in agony.

clue.text: Some of clergy readers forming circle

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A group of clergy and lay readers stands in a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A gyre is a circular or spiral motion, a ring forming in water or air.

clue.text: Tax this writer's column

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: this writer is = I am, I'M
a post is an upright column

explanation.surface: A journalist's column about taxation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'column' looks like a newspaper column; it is an upright POST.
explanation.definitionFit: An impost is a levy or duty imposed by authority.

clue.text: Laundry appliance no good with men's clothing

indicators.note: clothing something wraps it, so the men's letters go around the rest

parts.note: men's things are male

explanation.surface: An old laundry machine that is useless with menswear.
explanation.definitionFit: A mangle is a wringer with rollers for pressing water out of washed clothes.

clue.text: Young rascal placing bets loses second grand

indicators.note: losing something means it is removed; second says it is the later of the two matching letters that goes

parts.note: gaming is gambling, placing bets
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A young scamp gambling loses a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamin is a street urchin, a cheeky street child.

clue.text: Downgrading of French proposal

parts.note: de is French for of
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A French plan to cut someone's rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Demotion is a reduction in rank, a downgrading.

clue.text: Upright object supporting leg

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes second

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket, the half of the field behind the batsman's legs
an end is an object or aim

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture holding up a table leg, set vertically.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side, the side the batter's legs face, is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing on end means upright, vertical.

clue.text: One squad's short of a pair

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: short of something means lacking it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a team is a squad; the 's is just is

explanation.surface: A player's team is down two members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a pair' looks like what the squad lacks; only 'a' is lacking, and 'a pair' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple in a romantic relationship is called an item.

clue.text: Returning old pack, tore off a strip and added more

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the pack's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a bale is a bundled pack of goods
to rate is to scold, to tear a strip off someone

explanation.surface: Someone sends back an old parcel, rips off some tape and adds extra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns BALE into ELAB. 'Tear a strip off' is British slang for scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to add more detail to something.

clue.text: Brown beverage to take home from audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the letters are those of what is heard

parts.note: a brew is a drink such as tea or beer; to net is to take home as clear pay

explanation.surface: A brown drink to bring back from a stage try-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' looks like a stage try-out; it means hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunette describes brown hair, or a person with it.

clue.text: Philatelist ultimately understands stamps

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so take the last letter

parts.note: to read a situation is to understand it

explanation.surface: A stamp collector finally grasps stamps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stamps' looks like postage; it is the verb, to tread heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp is to put a foot down heavily, to tread.
